items.evidenceQuote: Governance Metadata + Enforcement Rules = Governed AI
items.imageObservation: The image shows a smiling woman with long dark hair, wearing a dark blazer and a dark top, standing indoors with a blurred background that includes a light-colored wall and a textured pillar.
items.text: A lot of people are scared of AI right now. They talk about AI like it is alive or unpredictable, but AI is not magic. AI is nothing without the records and the information that feed it. If the records are ungoverned, the behavior becomes unpredictable. If the records are governed, the behavior becomes controlled. Here is the formula: Governance Metadata + Enforcement Rules = Governed AI Governance metadata are the labels that tell AI what the information is, and how it must be treated. Enforcement rules are the instructions that tell AI what to do, and what not to do. When every record carries both, the entire system becomes a controlled environment. If every record inside an AI system is governed, the data is governed. If the data is governed, the information is governed. If the information is governed, the model is governed. AI cannot act outside the boundaries of the records it learns from. No structure means unpredictability. Unpredictability creates fear. Structure removes unpredictability. Structure removes fear. If structure is the key to controlling AI, AI does not need to be feared.
items.topicSummary: The post argues that AI unpredictability and fear can be mitigated through robust data governance, using a formula of governance metadata and enforcement rules applied to every record.
items.whySelected: The post's core formula provides a clear point of agreement, allowing for a constructive follow-up question about the practicalities of implementing such governance at an enterprise scale, which aligns with Balasubramaniam's expertise.

items.text: Agentic AI, explained on one whiteboard. Most people use "agents" as a buzzword. The board breaks it into 5 levels, and each level contains everything to its left. Level 1 is traditional machine learning. Learning patterns from data to make predictions, like a model that prices houses. Level 2 is enhanced ML. Same models, better results, through feature engineering, hyperparameter tuning, cross-validation, and ensembles. Level 3 is intelligent applications. Models deployed in real products with context and feedback. Real-time inference, data pipelines, monitoring, A/B testing. Think recommendation systems. Level 4 is autonomous agents. Systems that make decisions and act with limited human intervention. The core loop is perceive, decide, act, backed by goal setting, memory, and environment interaction. An auto-trading bot lives here. Level 5 is agentic systems. Fully autonomous systems that plan, learn, and pursue complex goals across domains. The loop upgrades to plan, execute, reflect, learn. Strategic planning, multi-step reasoning, tool use, self-improvement. An AI research assistant is the canonical example. Two things apply at every level. The principles nobody gets to skip. Safety, ethics, privacy, transparency, human in the loop. And the enablers nobody gets to skip either. Data quality, compute, MLOps, evals, and the talent to run it all. Success is simple to define. The system solves real problems, adapts to change, creates value, improves over time, and stays aligned with human goals. To go deeper: • AI Foundations for PMs: https://lnkd.in/e6zyYugs • AI Agents for PMs: https://lnkd.in/eeey5Cxr • Practical AI Agents: https://lnkd.in/eyamsW7a The whole board comes down to one line at the bottom. The goal was never just smarter models. Smarter systems win.
items.topicSummary: The post outlines a five-level framework for Agentic AI, progressing from traditional ML to fully autonomous systems, emphasizing that success lies in smarter systems, not just smarter models.
items.whySelected: The post's clear progression of AI capabilities provides a natural entry point to discuss the practical implications of increasing autonomy in an enterprise context, specifically around process and governance.
